title: One packet in two snapshots: staging keeps the first copy by received_at, core one row per position delivery
reasoning: Snapshots staging-fixture-a and staging-fixture-b overlap in time, so some deliveries are in both. A delivery present in two snapshots is one raw row in each (ing_01), with the received_at of its own capture.
Packet 1001: s01-m001 is in both snapshots, at 10:00:05 in a and 10:00:02 in b. stg_packet keeps the first copy by received_at, b's, so the later snapshot's copy wins when it is earlier (ing_06).

Packet 1002: s01-m002 is in both snapshots, at 11:00:01 in a and 11:00:04 in b; s01-m003 is a second delivery of the same packet at the same gateway under the MeshSTL broker's root, in b only, at 11:00:03. stg_packet keeps a's s01-m002, the first of the three (ing_06).

Packet 1004 is a Position from s01-r, uplinked by itself, in both snapshots: 09:05:10 in a, 09:05:07 in b. stg_packet keeps b's copy. stg_position keeps both raw rows, one per snapshot, and fct_node_position keeps one row for the delivery, b's, the first by received_at.
s01-m005 has no packet_id, so its copies are told apart by delivery_key alone: it is in both snapshots, 12:00:00 in a and 12:00:01 in b, and stg_packet keeps a's.

Packet 1006 from s01-r was heard by two gateways, s01-g (s01-m006) and s01-h (s01-m007), in snapshot a. They are copies of one packet at two different gateways, so stg_packet keeps both (ing_06 deduplicates per gateway).

s01-m008 is a second delivery from s01-r at s01-g without packet_id, in snapshot a only, distinct from s01-m005. Without packet_id two deliveries cannot be shown to be one packet, so stg_packet keeps both s01-m005 and s01-m008.

s01-m009 is a 20-bit Position from s01-r in both snapshots: at 09:10:00 in a, carried by the public broker only, and at 09:10:03 in b, carried by the MeshSTL broker only. stg_packet and core keep a's copy, the first. pos_04 flags a position when seen_meshstl is true on its delivery; read as any copy of the delivery in any snapshot (Casey, issue #55 comment 6985802330, item 7: "(a), any copy in any snapshot"), the delivery was carried by MeshSTL, so core's seen_meshstl and precise_source are true while a's own row in stg_position says false.
stg_packet therefore holds exactly eight rows of this case: (b, s01-m001), (a, s01-m002), (b, s01-m004), (a, s01-m005), (a, s01-m006), (a, s01-m007), (a, s01-m008) and (a, s01-m009).

This is the test item 7 asks for, a later snapshot's MeshSTL copy updating a row core already keeps: the fixture build loads snapshot a, builds core with a's public copy of s01-m009 kept and precise_source false, then loads snapshot b and runs dbt incrementally, after which assert_pos_02_fixture_positions_in_core requires the kept row, still a's copy, to carry seen_meshstl and precise_source true; the full refresh after it must give the same row.

Expected positions, by hand: s01-m004 and s01-m009 are 20-bit cells near 38.60 N, 90.37 W, usable and inside the MSA. Core keeps b's copy of s01-m004 (09:05:07, earlier) and a's copy of s01-m009 (09:10:00, earlier). s01-m004 was public on both copies: never precise. s01-m009's b copy alone is precise in staging; core's flag is true by the any-copy reading.
